* A Russian glide-bomb attack struck Kharkiv in the early hours, smashing into a residential building and a nearby playground. Seven people were killed, and at least 77 others were injured. Among the dead was a 14-year-old girl, according to Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskiy. Rescue teams worked through broken concrete and twisted metal as they searched for anyone trapped beneath the wreckage. A woman’s body was later pulled from the ruins, raising the death toll. About 20 of the injured remained in severe condition, said the regional governor, Oleh Syniehubov. Residents described scenes of panic as dust and smoke filled the street.  

* Ukrainian authorities said the assault involved five aerial guided glide bombs launched from planes based in Russia’s Belgorod region. Zelenskiy said the attack showed why Ukraine needs greater control over long-range weapons. He renewed his call on western partners to let Ukraine strike Russian airbases used for such attacks. “A strike … would not have happened if our defence forces had the ability to destroy Russian military aircraft where they are based,” he said. He added that there was no rational reason to restrict Ukraine’s defences. The statement reflected mounting frustration in Kyiv as Russian air attacks continue to hit homes, schools, and public spaces.  

* In Belgorod, Russian officials gave a different account and said Ukraine had fired cluster munitions into the city and surrounding suburbs. Regional governor Vyacheslav Gladkov said at least five people were killed and 37 civilians were wounded, including at least six children. He said one woman and four men died of their wounds before an ambulance arrived. Gladkov posted a video showing a house on fire. Local crews moved quickly to secure the area and protect nearby streets. The blast reportedly damaged vehicles, windows, and power lines across several blocks.  

* The dual claims from Kyiv and Moscow highlighted the grim rhythm of the war, in which each side accuses the other of harming civilians. In Kharkiv, families gathered near cordoned-off streets, hoping to learn whether relatives were safe. In Belgorod, neighbors tried to help one another as emergency crews treated the wounded. A damaged communications tower briefly disrupted mobile reception in part of the area, adding to the confusion after the strike. Officials on both sides used the incidents to push their political messages. Yet on the ground, the immediate reality was smoke, sirens, and shattered homes.  

* By nightfall, volunteers and rescue workers were still sorting through debris in Kharkiv and assessing damage in Belgorod. Medical staff continued to treat the injured, many of whom had been rushed to hospitals by ambulance. The attacks deepened fear among civilians who have lived under repeated bombardment for months. Parents kept children close, and apartment residents checked basements and shelters for safer places to wait. The war’s reach, from residential streets to public squares, remained painfully visible. As the fighting continued, both cities faced the same burden: rebuilding after violence that seemed to arrive without warning.
